parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Determine, for this nuclear reaction, the value of $x$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Show that the energy equivalent to $1.00\text{ u}$ is $934\text{ MeV}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the energy, in $\text{MeV}$, released in this reaction. Give your answer to three significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Suggest the forms of energy into which the energy calculated in (b)(ii) is transformed.

stem:
One possible nuclear reaction that takes place in a nuclear reactor is given by the equation

$$^{235}_{92}\text{U} + ^{1}_{0}\text{n} \rightarrow ^{95}_{42}\text{Mo} + ^{139}_{57}\text{La} + 2^{1}_{0}\text{n} + x^{0}_{-1}\text{e}$$

Data for the nuclei and particles are given in Fig. 12.1.

| nucleus or particle | mass / u |
| --- | --- |
| $^{235}_{92}\text{U}$ | 235.123 |
| $^{95}_{42}\text{Mo}$ | 94.945 |
| $^{139}_{57}\text{La}$ | 138.955 |
| $^{1}_{0}\text{n}$ | 1.00863 |
| $^{0}_{-1}\text{e}$ | $5.49 \times 10^{-4}$ |
